anatomy.flutter: InputGroup(child, startAddon, endAddon, invalid, enabled, focusNode, disabledReason) builds a _GroupScope > Row[startAddon?, Expanded(child), endAddon?] and paints the pill via nested TweenAnimationBuilder<Color?> into a Surface; InputGroupInput/InputGroupAddon/InputGroupText/InputGroupButton are the companion slot widgets.
anatomy.web: InputGroup is a <div role="group" data-slot="input-group"> whose own class list paints the pill directly (has-[...]-driven focus/invalid rings), with InputGroupAddon/InputGroupButton/InputGroupText/InputGroupInput/InputGroupTextarea as sibling DOM children selected by CSS `has-*`/`data-align` — the same five-part anatomy, CSS-selector-driven on the web and InheritedWidget-driven in Flutter.

api.flutter: InputGroup exposes only child + startAddon + endAddon (two fixed named slots) plus invalid/enabled/focusNode/disabledReason; InputGroupInput takes controller/initialValue/placeholder/onChanged/onSubmitted/readOnly/obscureText/keyboardType/autofillHints/textSpec/label but NOT the block-start/block-end orientation.
api.web: InputGroupAddon's `align` variant is a real four-way enum — "inline-start" | "inline-end" | "block-start" | "block-end" — and the group's own class list carries has-[>[data-align=block-end]]:flex-col / has-[>[data-align=block-start]]:flex-col to turn the whole pill into a column layout (input-group.tsx:34-37); InputGroupTextarea is also a first-class exported control, letting a group wrap a multi-line field.
api.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The Dart doc comment for InputGroupAlign (input_group.dart:487-496) explicitly records this: 'The two block values (block-start/block-end, which turn the group into a column) are not reached by either ported page and are not built.' There is no InputGroupTextarea port either — InputGroup's child slot is typed Widget and only ever holds an InputGroupInput on the ported pages. A group wrapping a Textarea, or stacking an addon above/below the control, has no Flutter equivalent at all.

states.flutter: _InputGroupState tracks _focusWithin via a non-focusable Focus(canRequestFocus: false, onFocusChange: _setFocusWithin) node, and paints border/ring from invalid > focusWithin > rest, with `has-disabled:opacity-50` reproduced as Disabled(disabled: !enabled) — matching rest/focus-within/invalid/disabled.
states.web: Same four states plus the combobox integration: `in-data-[slot=combobox-content]:focus-within:border-inherit in-data-[slot=combobox-content]:focus-within:ring-0` (input-group.tsx:17) suppresses the group's own focus ring when it is rendered inside a Combobox popover, so the popover's own chrome does not get double-ringed.

This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. ORIGINAL: The `in-data-[slot=combobox-content]:` state override has no Flutter counterpart — InputGroup always paints its own focus-within ring regardless of an ancestor Combobox, because Flutter's InheritedWidget/Focus plumbing has no equivalent of a CSS `:has()`/`in-*` ancestor-context selector. This is unreached on the ported pages (input_group.dart's own JSDoc records the group as unreached inside a combobox), so it is a latent rather than a demonstrated gap.

disabled.flutter: group = Disabled(disabled: !enabled, reason: widget.disabledReason ?? field?.disabledReason, child: group) — opacity halves via the shared Disabled widget, and the doc comment notes the control inside keeps its own disabled:opacity-45 as well, so the two opacities multiply exactly as the two class lists do on the web.
disabled.web: `has-disabled:opacity-50` on the group multiplies with the control's own `disabled:opacity-45` (or `disabled:opacity-50` on the bare Input) since both are real CSS opacity layers on nested elements — the input_group.dart comment explicitly calls out this multiplication as intentional and unreached on both ported pages.

interaction.flutter: InputGroupAddon wires GestureDetector(onTap: group?.controlFocusNode.requestFocus) over the whole addon padding box, and relies on Flutter's gesture arena (innermost recognizer wins) to let a nested InputGroupButton's own tap take priority — reproducing the web's e.target.closest("button") opt-out without needing the DOM check.
interaction.web: InputGroupAddon's onClick handler explicitly checks `(e.target as HTMLElement).closest("button")` and returns early so a button click is never redirected to focus the control (input-group.tsx:57-62); otherwise `e.currentTarget.parentElement?.querySelector("input")?.focus()` focuses the field.

semantics.flutter: Semantics(container: true, child: group) on InputGroup and Semantics(container: true, child: addon) on InputGroupAddon reproduce role="group" on both the group and each addon, without inventing an accessible name for either.
semantics.web: InputGroup renders role="group" explicitly (input-group.tsx:15); InputGroupAddon also renders role="group" (line 53) — matching containers on both sides, neither naming itself.
